NDIA ICT Integration Policy
NDIA-POL-ICT-ING-001
Integration
1. Purpose, authority and permitted exchange
Statutory purpose and lawful information exchange

NDIA integrations must be used only where they support NDIA statutory functions or an approved data sharing purpose, have a documented lawful authority, and enforce technical and procedural controls that prevent unauthorised collection, use, disclosure, caching, transformation, reuse or exchange of protected Agency information and barred data.

NDIA must only build, run or use an integration when it supports an NDIA function or an approved data sharing purpose and has a clear legal authority. Integrations must not collect, use, disclose, store, transform or share protected information unless that authority and the approved purpose allow it.
Mandatory statutory requirement
Critical

2. Governance, risk ownership and accountability
Governance, risk ownership and shared accountability

Every integration must have named business, system and security risk owners, be assessed against NDIA's approved governance arrangements and enterprise risk appetite, and allocate shared risk, control, monitoring, training, escalation and review responsibilities across NDIA and connected partners.

Each integration must have a named business owner, system owner and security risk owner before design or operation starts. Owners must understand the shared risks, agree controls with partners, monitor those controls and review accountability regularly.

3. Secure lifecycle and authorisation gates
Security lifecycle, authorisation, asset register and change control

Integrations must follow an ISM-aligned secure lifecycle from design to decommissioning, document architecture, control mapping and risk assessment, meet the approved Essential Eight target or obtain formal risk acceptance, and must not operate or materially change until residual risk is accepted by the Authorising Officer and the integration is recorded in the authorised systems or interface register.

Every integration must follow a secure lifecycle from design to retirement. It must be documented, risk assessed, recorded in the approved register, meet the agreed Essential Eight target or have a formal risk acceptance, and receive authorisation before it goes live or materially changes.
Mandatory security governance requirement
Critical

4. Classification, markings and caveats
Classification, protective markings, metadata and caveat handling

Integration payloads, messages, records, logs and metadata must preserve security classifications, protective markings, caveats and access-restriction metadata, and must enforce need-to-know, clearance or eligibility, routing and recipient controls appropriate to the highest sensitivity or classification of the data, including AUSTEO, AGAO and foreign-origin information.

Integrations must keep security classifications, protective markings, caveats and access restrictions with the data as it moves between systems. Access, routing, recipients and logging must be based on the most sensitive data in the integration.
Mandatory information protection requirement
Critical

5. Sharing agreements and cross-border exchange
Information-sharing agreements, DATA Scheme controls and foreign/cross-border exchange

Before sharing data through an integration with another government, external, foreign or international party, NDIA must confirm the lawful sharing pathway, approved agreement or Data Sharing Agreement, participant accreditation where required, cross-border safeguards, foreign-interference and sovereignty risk treatment, authorised recipients, purpose, controls, retention and incident obligations, and must implement these requirements in technical release gates.

NDIA must not share data with an external, foreign or international party through an integration until the lawful pathway, approved agreement, recipients, purpose, retention, safeguards and incident obligations are documented and built into the integration controls.
Mandatory data sharing requirement
Critical

6. Privacy and sensitive identifiers
Privacy, personal information, identifiers and sensitive health/identity data

Integrations involving personal information, health information, healthcare identifiers, government identifiers, Digital ID attributes or biometric and restricted identity data must complete privacy-by-design assessment, collect, use or disclose only approved fields for an authorised purpose, issue required notices or consent controls, protect information in transit, at rest and in logs, limit retention or de-identify it, restrict and review access, and prohibit My Health Record or restricted data handling unless expressly authorised and approved.

Integrations that handle personal, health, identity, Digital ID, biometric or other sensitive data must apply privacy by design. They must use only the minimum approved fields, give required notices or consent choices, protect data in transit, at rest and in logs, restrict access, and retain or de-identify data only as approved.
Mandatory privacy requirement
Critical

7. Secure engineering and monitoring controls
Secure engineering controls, identity, secrets, encryption and monitoring

Integration code, platforms, identities, credentials, endpoints and data flows must implement secure engineering and control baselines, including secure development, dependency and configuration checks, unique least-privilege identities, approved secret and token handling, encryption and managed keys, gateway and boundary protections, logging and monitoring, Protective DNS or equivalent malicious-endpoint controls, vulnerability disclosure and remediation, cryptography readiness and cyber threat intelligence integration where applicable.

Integration platforms, code and interfaces must be securely designed, built, tested and operated. They must use approved identity, least privilege, secrets management, encryption, gateway controls, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management and threat detection.

8. API and digital service design
API design, interoperability, reuse and service consistency

NDIA integrations and APIs must use approved Australian Government and NDIA design patterns, including OpenAPI specifications, catalogue registration, reusable interfaces where safe and lawful, consistent naming, payload, pagination, error, versioning and lifecycle patterns, controlled change and deprecation, and connection patterns that reduce repeat data requests and support reliable digital services.

APIs and integrations must use approved government and NDIA design patterns so they are secure, consistent, reusable and easy to support. They must be registered, documented with OpenAPI or equivalent specifications, versioned, tested and decommissioned using a controlled process.

9. Cloud, hosting and regulated infrastructure
Cloud, hosting, gateway, regulated infrastructure and resilience

Integrations using cloud, hosting, gateways, Security Service Edge, data centres, connected devices or regulated critical infrastructure services must use approved or certified providers where required, review current IRAP or equivalent assurance, define shared cloud controls and sovereignty or data residency risks, protect internet-connected and classified flows through approved gateway or SSE capabilities, maintain exit, portability and continuity arrangements, identify SOCI and Systems of Government Significance obligations and third-party data processing notifications, and include critical assets in required risk management programs.

Integrations hosted in cloud, gateway, data centre, regulated infrastructure or connected-device environments must use approved hosting and security arrangements. NDIA must confirm assurance, shared controls, data location, resilience, exit and continuity requirements before use.
Mandatory hosting and resilience requirement
Critical
